page: Microsoft Azure DS4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DS family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz. The configuration includes 8 dedicated physical cores with 1.0 thread per core, providing 8 vCPUs. The CPU is equipped with a 35 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache. It supports hardware instructions such as AVX, AVX-512, AES cryptography, and FMA.

The server is provisioned with 28.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 3.5 GB per core. Local storage is limited to a bundled 57 GB volume, and the instance does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, including stress-ng, Geekbench, and single-threaded gzip compression, consistently fall into the bottom 25% tier. Conversely, multi-core execution, such as multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU tests, registers in the middle 50% average tier. Memory bandwidth tests, including cached small-block reads at 720.11 GB/sec and uncached large-block reads at 81.38 GB/sec, also align with average tier expectations.

Given its balanced resource profile and average multi-core capabilities, the DS4 is positioned for general-purpose workloads, software compilation, and basic database operations. Its qualitative cost efficiency is characterized by a moderate resource density that balances dedicated CPU cores with standard memory allocations, though workloads requiring high single-thread performance or local storage capacity may face performance tradeoffs.
description: Microsoft Azure DS4 is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores (8 vCPUs), 28.0 GB of memory, and 57 GB of local storage. Performance benchmarks indicate weak single-core capabilities, placing in the bottom 25% for single-threaded tasks. However, multi-core performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations consistently rank in the average middle 50% tier, with cached small-block memory reads reaching 720.11 GB/sec. Lacking GPU acceleration and public IPv4 addresses, this instance is designed for balanced workloads such as software compilation, static web serving, and moderate database operations where multi-threaded execution can offset the lower single-core speeds.
